away.headline: NC State loses 2 players for the season, several are questionable. Who's injured?
away.blurb: Head coach Dave Doeren said Monday that offensive lineman Yousef Mugharbil and tight end Vander Ploog are out for the season. Mugharbil sustained a lower leg injury during the Wolfpack’s 31-28 win over Louisville. He recorded a 64.4 offensive grade, according to Pro Football Focus, which was third on the offensive line. Mugharbil also graded out at 70 in pass blocking. The former transfer walk-on put together his best season of college football, earning a career-high 339 snaps. Ploog, a sophomore transfer from Oregon, played eight snaps against Virginia and one against Richmond. He came to Raleigh with a nagging shoulder injury, Doeren said, and could not get healthy. He will be able to return, but it won’t be until after the conclusion of this season. Ploog was spotted prior to the bye week leaving practice in a sling. Sowells was ruled out prior to the Wake Forest game. Doeren said Sowells will have a repair done and return to activities after his rehab is complete. He reiterated that the team hoped the center would be available this season, but the medical staff did not feel like it would make enough progress in the time frame remaining. Richardson was ruled out after the season opener. He sustained a season-ending bicep injury against Virginia and underwent surgery. N.C. State retakes the field this week following its second bye, but the roster continues to take hits. “Feel terrible for him,” Doeren said on Monday. “He was playing so good, and has been such a great leader on our offensive line, and has been through a lot. For those of you that know his story, it’s pretty significant what he went through at Florida. Good news is he has a year to recover fully and have a great season next year. But, in the moment, it hurts to lose such a good player on the offensive line.” Mugharbil collided with a semi-truck during his freshman year at Florida, days before the Gators’ season opener, ending his rookie season. He did not see game action during his time in Gainesville. Mugharbil transferred to Colorado but left shortly after arriving in Boulder. He returned to North Carolina and walked on with the Wolfpack before earning a scholarship and starting job. Offensive lineman Kamen Smith, wide receiver Jojo Trader, running back Duke Scott and safety Tristan Teasdell are also day-to-day. The latter three were injured against the Cardinals. Scott leads the Wolfpack in rushing yards (358) and was ranked No. 33 in the country prior to the Louisville game. The junior has two 100-yard games, including a 148-yard performance against Appalachian State. Teasdell has 17 tackles this season and played 173 snaps in five appearances. Trader played 161 snaps in five games and recorded 221 receiving yards. Finally, Smith played 361 snaps in five games and has been one of the most consistent players on offense, according to PFF. away.headline: NC State vs. Stanford injury report: Duke Scott among many players out
away.blurb: Yousef Mugharbil joined the out-for-season list after the injury he suffered against Louisville, which is a bummer for a guy who has already been through a lot to get back to a point where he’s making an impact on the field. Jimarion McCrimon isn’t listed at all on the report this week, so that’s a positive development, but Kamen Smith is questionable again. Working with a patchwork line is a little easier against the likes of Stanford than Wake or Louisville, at least. Has NC State’s injury situation improved after a week off? No, not really. In addition to missing at least two starting linemen, State will again be without running back Duke Scott, so that’s unfortunate. Not as unfortunate as the Pack’s dilapidated ground game, but not far off. Stanford’s most notable injured player is linebacker Matt Rose, who was a second-team All-ACC player in 2025 after racking up 106 tackles. He hasn’t played in a game for the Cardinal since the last week of September.

picks.headline: Indiana’s Curt Cignetti gives prediction on Michigan starting QB, talks impressive Wolverines
picks.blurb: Defending national champion Indiana is coming off a 19-15 loss to Ohio State that easily could have gone the other way. Now, the Hoosiers will head north to take on Michigan at The Big House, with the Wolverines coming off a 21-18 victory over Penn State. “Out of the frying pan, into the fire, as we get ready for Michigan,” Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti , the reigning back-to-back AP coach of the year, said at his Monday press conference. “Impressive team, especially on defense.” Michigan made a quarterback change from sophomore Bryce Underwood to freshman Tommy Carr at halftime of the win over the Nittany Lions, and head coach Kyle Whittingham has opted not to name a starter for this weekend’s game. “Really tough opponent this week, Michigan,” Cignetti said. “Made a quarterback change in the second half against Penn State. Gave them a shot in the arm, scored three second-half touchdowns to win the game. “Really impressed with their defense, their quickness, their tenacity, the way they play, play in and play out, the way they run to the ball. This is a top-flight defense. “Offensively, they’re got good running backs. Quarterback came in, played really well. The other quarterback has a cannon and can run, makes a lot of plays with his legs. So they’ll be feeling pretty good about themselves after that victory. “It’ll be a very physical football game again, our eighth game in a row. “Looking forward here, not backward. And this will be a very tough challenge.” Here’s what else Cignetti said about Michigan heading into Saturday’s game: Indiana looking to get its run game going “Teams like Ohio State, Michigan, they don’t get up much rushing yardage. We did have some positive runs. We got into kind of a throw mode — I think we called 46 passes and 26 runs — which is very uncharacteristic of us. “It all starts up front. And we all want more consistent production and explosive plays. We haven’t gotten the explosive plays the last two weeks.” On if he will watch high school film on Tommy Carr “You can see what you need to see in the second half of Penn State, in my opinion, which I watched. “I’d assume it would be him. It could be two quarterbacks on the field at the same time. That would not surprise me. They did that at Utah. And the other guy can make plays. “Schematically, they didn’t change a whole lot in the second half.” On playing multiple physical games in a row with no bye week yet “We try to keep them healthy and fresh the best we can the entire season. At this point in the year, there might be a slight tweak, but not major.”

away.headline: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide the Buckeyes' season
away.blurb: But that stride was debilitating. Marsh's left foot came down out of bounds, and he knew it immediately. The look on his face was heartbreaking. That misery wasn't felt on the Ohio State sideline. Instead, it was relief, but with questions about what's to come. The primary reason Indiana had a chance to win the game late was that Ohio State's starting QB Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with an apparent right arm injury earlier in the fourth quarter. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said after the game, without going into specifics about the injury, that Sayin would be out "several weeks." The good news is Ohio State is off next week. The bad news is that when the Buckeyes return from their respite, they'll be on the road to face USC , and then it's a home game with Oregon . While both those teams have had their issues in 2026, the prospect of having to face both with a true freshman at QB is not one that should excite anybody in Scarlet and Gray. If Sayin is out even longer, there are games left against a Northwestern team that's now 5-1 after beating Michigan State , as well as a road game against the Nebraska team that gave Indiana fits last week. Oh, and there's Michigan too. College football can be a brutal sport. Sometimes victory can be taken from you by a toe or two; other times, it comes at a serious cost. That was the case Saturday in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana , a game neither team escaped feeling whole. Indiana's 22-game win streak came to an end in an extremely painful manner. Down five late, on a fourth-and-4 at the Ohio State 27, Indiana opted to go for the throat instead of the first down. Josh Hoover dropped back, found a wide-open Nick Marsh down the sideline, and hit him in stride. After taking a vicious hit from Indiana's Mario Landino, Sayin was seen running to the Ohio State locker room, right arm hanging by his side. He emerged a few minutes later with it in a sling, as the diminutive true freshman Luke Fahey filled in for him, and the Buckeyes offense ground to a complete halt. The Buckeyes didn't manage a first down with Fahey in the game, so while they survived the trip to Bloomington, got revenge on the Hoosiers for last season's Big Ten Championship, and avoided a perilous second loss, there are suddenly concerning questions lingering around the program. While Buckeyes fans everywhere celebrate this win, they'll do so while awaiting an injury report that could determine the fate of their season.

home.headline: Michigan injury updates: Rod Moore ‘OK’ after being carted off in win
home.blurb: The Wolverines were down a second starting offensive lineman, guard Brady Norton, while center Jake Guarnera and guard Nathan Efobi both played through injuries in Saturday’s 21-18 victory at Michigan Stadium . Guarnera especially, having been listed as a game-time decision two hours before kickoff. “Everyone has something going on at this point in the season,” starting tackle Blake Frazier said. “I’m super proud of him. He was straining all week to make sure that he was giving himself the best opportunity to be out there with us today.” ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Michigan football continues to limp its way through the schedule, and the win over Penn State was no different. Michigan (4-2, 1-2 Big Ten) started backup Avery Gach at right guard while welcoming sixth offensive lineman Manuel Beigel back to the lineup. The Wolverines were able to run for a season-high 211 yards and three touchdowns, much of that coming in the second half with backup Tommy Carr at quarterback. In-game, though, the Wolverines had to deal with a couple of scares. Safety Rod Moore had to be carted off the field in the third quarter after intercepting a Rocco Becht pass; his first turnover of the season. “Should be OK,” Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham said. “It’s nothing major. Now, will he be ready for the next game? That’s debatable, but it’s nothing that’s long term.” That’s good news for Moore, who returned in full this season following a two-year rehab from a torn ACL and meniscus in his knee. He’s started all six games this season and is one of two captains on defense. Meanwhile, cornerback Jyaire Hill was missing in the secondary toward the end of the game, and Whittingham suggested an injury kept him from playing. “But it doesn’t appear to be anything — kind of like Rod — long term,” Whittingham said. Hill struggled in coverage against Penn State receiver Chase Sowell, who caught 11 passes for 151 yards and a touchdown and drew a pair of holding penalties against the senior defensive back. “That receiver is a good receiver,” Whittingham said. “A big, physical kid. I thought we were a little soft in pass defense this game. We needed to get up and challenge a little more, get in the receiver’s face and be a little bit more aggressive in that respect.” To illustrate how beaten up Michigan is, Whittingham said as many as six starters would have been sidelined last week had the Wolverines played a game. They were on a bye instead, giving the team enough time to get some players back in time. “It was good to get those guys healthy and be able to get them to this game and perform,” Whittingham said. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. picks.blurb: Auburn is ready to return to its home field after pulling off one of college football's most stunning upsets in Week 7 over then-No. 1 Georgia. Auburn won the turnover battle, 3-0, and ran the football efficiently, outgaining the Bulldogs, 192-113, in what was arguably its cleanest game of the season. LSU bounced back from Week 6's loss at Kentucky by shutting out then-No. 19 Mississippi State in Baton Rouge, 31-0. The Tigers took advantage of a Kamario Taylor-less Mississippi State squad, outgaining them, 379-291. This week marks the second straight week Auburn has had to prepare for a top SEC squad in terms of production. LSU is the SEC-best in total offense (504 yards per game), defense (256.4 yards allowed per game), first downs (28 per game), and passing (308 yards per game). The Bayou Bengals rank in the top five in several other categories, including points per game, points allowed per game, and time of possession. However, Auburn proved in Athens last week that stats do not matter and that being more physical can be enough to win. A key storyline to follow is the battle between two first-year head coaches, Alex Golesh and Lane Kiffin. Kiffin is 2-3 against Auburn as a head coach, and has won his last two games against the Tigers (2022 and 2023 at Ole Miss). Golesh has never faced Kiffin as a head coach. Another storyline is the rivalry renewal between two old-school SEC West teams. Auburn and LSU have not played since the 2023 season, and LSU leads the series, 30-24-1 over Auburn . away.blurb: The first injury report for Mississippi State at LSU football dropped Wednesday night. It listed a handful of significant names. Most notably, Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor is questionable. Mississippi State RB Fluff Bothwell is also questionable. Bothwell is averaging over five yards per carry. The veteran back is a go-to option for Jeff Lebby's offense. Mississippi State linebacker Jalen Smith was listed as out, meaning the Bulldogs will be down a starter on defense. Mississippi State won't get much sympathy from an LSU team also dealing with the injury bug. LSU stars Trey'Dez Green and Whit Weeks remained sidelined and aren't expected back until November. Hybrid defensive back Da'Shawn Spears tore his ACL vs. Ole Miss and remains out for the year. LSU WR Phillip Wright and LB Charles Ross are also out for the year. Neither was a starter, but both saw rotational playing time and made impacts on special teams. Taylor left Mississippi State's Week 5 contest vs. Alabama (MSU was on bye in Week 6) with a lower-body injury. Earlier this week, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Taylor's status was in flux. The betting spread has moved in LSU's favor since the opening line, indicating bettors think Taylor may not play. Taylor, one of the country's best quarterbacks, would be a significant loss for Mississippi State. The offense runs through Taylor, and the dynamic QB was generating Heisman buzz earlier this year. LSU vs. Mississippi State is set for this Saturday at 11 AM in Tiger Stadium. Tiger Rag Magazine Digital Issue – August 2026 – Football Season Guide Tiger Rag Magazine Digital Edition – February 2026 Tiger Rag Magazine Digital Edition – January 2026 By GLENN GUILBEAU, Tiger Rag Editor LSU wide receiver Jackson Harris is one player you will likely not see on the Tigers' injury report to be released by the Southeastern Conference office on Wednesday. Harris, who later wore a protective walking boot on Saturday, leads LSU in receiving yards with 456 this season on 27 catches. The junior transfer from Hawaii also is first in touchdown catches with five and in average yards per catch among those who have caught more than three passes at 16.9. “The more passes he throws me and the more plays I make, the more he's going to trust me to make that play on critical downs and when we need plays,” Harris said. “I'm just really happy for him.” Leavitt is coming off of one of his best games as he completed 31 of 38 passes for 289 yards and a season-high four touchdowns. “He's just a gamer,” Harris said. Harris has also noticed that about running back Dilin Jones. “Every time he gets the ball, he's dropping somebody,” Harris said of Jones, who rushed 18 times for 84 yards and caught eight passes for 58 yards with 54 of those coming after contact. “He makes somebody fall every time. He's NOT going down on the first guy. So if you see your teammate playing that hard, it just matters more to him. So it's going to matter more to you. You want to block for him. We can count on him in every situation.” Harris ran much like Jones when he caught a short pass from Leavitt and made it a 27-yard touchdown in the first quarter after he bulldozed his way through several tacklers near the goal line. “It's really just a mindset,” Harris said. “Like Dilin's always fighting for those extra yards, so I just made the decision to get in the end zone.

home.headline: Georgia football injury report: Another starter ruled out for Auburn
home.blurb: Starting Georgia safety KJ Bolden is officially out for Saturday’s clash with Auburn in the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry. In Friday’s SEC Availability Report , the Bulldogs downgraded Bolden from doubtful to out. Georgia ruled out junior wideout Isiah Canion , sophomore wideout Thomas Blackshear , junior running back Chauncey Bowens , junior EDGE Amaris Williams and freshman defensive back Tyriq Green on Wednesday with the first report of the week. With Canion out, Blackshear had taken on a bigger role, that was until he suffered a collarbone injury in the Vanderbilt game. The Savannah native caught three passes for 33 yards before leaving the game. Blackshear started his first game in Week 4 vs. Oklahoma. Green should be nearing a return after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 2. Green suffered the injury shortly after returning a 93-yard kickoff for a touchdown. He underwent tightrope surgery, but Georgia has no need to rush him back. Green was the Bulldogs’ top kick returner through the first two games. After suffering a torn ACL in spring drills, Williams is likely out for the entire regular season. However, he could return for the postseason. Bowens had Lisfranc surgery and is likely done for the rest of the season. He sustained that injury in Georgia’s win over Vanderbilt in Week 5. Bolden came off the field slowly late in Georgia’s win over Alabama after tallying 7 tackles (3 solo), a half tackle for loss and a half sack. After the game, he was wearing a heavy wrap around his left calf muscle. Bolden’s streak of 34 straight games played to start his Georgia career is in jeopardy. He has started 19 of the last 20, missing one first half due to a targeting penalty in the previous game. Frazier, who hasn’t played since Week 3 against Arkansas, is not listed at all. Bolden is a new addition, but he’s battling a lower-body injury. Canion is in line to miss his fourth straight game with a bone bruise in his knee. He traveled to Arkansas last month as Georgia opened SEC play and got the start. He left that game in the opening series after aggravating the injury. The former Georgia Tech standout hasn’t played since. The Bulldogs and Tigers tee it up at 3:30 p.m. ET on ESPN. Georgia will enjoy its only bye of the season in Week 8.

home.headline: Georgia football injury report vs. Auburn
Georgia Injury Report Ahead of Auburn Game Reveals Troubling Reality with RB Room
home.blurb: As it turns out though, Kirby Smart's team is going to be a little bit banged up as they try to avoid a first home defeat against Auburn in more than two decades. As was the case last week, the running back room is going to be a bit thin. With the reporting around Chauncey Bowens as murky as ever, he has been ruled out for the second straight week and could wind up missing more time than that. Bowens is ruled out along with Isiah Canion, who has not seen much work this season. Thomas Blackshear is also out once again, but this is not a huge surprise. The bigger surprising thing is KJ Bolden being listed as questionable, potentially banged up from the Alabama game but dealing with an unknown injury. Reports from Pete Thamel of ESPN indicated that while Nate Frazier is not on the injury report, he was not last week either but still did not end up playing in the win over Alabama. Regardless, it looks like it could be a significant opportunity once again for guys like Dwight Phillips Jr. and Bo Walker to tote the rock and showcase the depth that Georgia has at the position. Given what the Dawgs proved against the Crimson Tide, they should be able to run the ball with success once again versus Auburn even without Bowens and likely Frazier as well. As Georgia tries to stay undefeated and keep the winning streak against Auburn alive, there is going to be serious urgency from this team to play as well as they did last week, which can often be difficult to replicate. If Gunner Stockton can keep up his strong level of play, this Dawgs team is going to be tough for anyone they face to have a real chance of winning. Once again though, he is going to be doing it with a little bit of a shorthanded running back room. As for what that means moving forward for the rest of the season, it remains to be seen, but Georgia certainly passed the first test with a depleted running back room. Time will tell if they can pass the next one as well.

picks.headline: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams
picks.blurb: Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings World Series preview Champions League results J.J. McCarthy starting for Giants NBA breakout candidates Can Tennessee football avoid letdown at South Carolina, other SEC picks | Adams John Adams, Knoxville News Sentinel Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:06 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Georgia's Kirby Smart has won so much for so long that he's regarded as the best coach in college football . But after a last-second loss to Auburn, he proved he can also be one of the sport's best quotes. "Humility is a week away," he said. Tennessee coach Josh Heupel would be wise to paraphrase Smart's comment before the Vols take on South Carolina at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia. The Vols are coming off a dominant 26-10 victory over Alabama . They're 6-1 and on the cusp of the top 10. But all they gained from a victory over their archrival could be lost with a loss to the unranked Gamecocks. Tennessee 26, South Carolina 16: In an unpredictable SEC season, team performances have varied drastically from one Saturday to the next. Based on that trend, Tennessee could be next in line to take a tumble after a big win. But amid all the SEC's inconsistency, UT's defense has remained steadfast. Something else to consider: Tennessee has been coming on strong in the second half; in South Carolina's last five SEC games dating back to last season, it has lost leads of 27, 16 and 17 points. LSU 31, Auburn 23: While I believe Tennessee's defense will prevent a letdown against South Carolina, I'm not as confident about Auburn's chances for prosperity after upsetting No. 1 Georgia. The LSU offense hasn't always been the model of consistency, but neither has Auburn's. LSU's challenge: Winning on the road. It already has lost at Ole Miss and Kentucky. That's a carryover from the Brian Kelly era. The Tigers lost all four of their SEC road games in 2025. They also lost their last two conference road games in 2024. So, they will take an eight-game SEC road losing streak with them to Jordan-Hare Stadium. They're due. Alabama 30, Texas A&M 15: The Tide also are due for a win after losing back-to-back games against Georgia and Tennessee. They can be grateful that their schedule offers a home game against the three-loss Aggies, who have lost two SEC games by 21 or more points. Texas A&M's 41-0 victory over The Citadel hardly qualifies as the beginning of a turnaround. However, it at least demonstrated that the Aggies aren't devoid of young talent. Freshman running back KJ Edwards led Texas A&M with 116 yards rushing on 16 carries. Freshman wide receiver Aaron Gregory led the Aggies' injury-depleted receiving corps with six catches for 94 yards. Oklahoma 23, Mississippi State 20: This matchup is all about quarterbacks. You can't be sure if Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor is healthy enough to play. Without him, Mississippi State lost 31-0 to LSU. With him, it scored 38 points against Minnesota and 41 on South Carolina. The health of Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer isn't an issue. Performance is his problem. Mateer is a fiery competitor and a running threat. But he doesn't protect the football. He has lost two fumbles and thrown seven interceptions in six games. And he has thrown only two more touchdown passes than interceptions. In Mateer's last season at Washington State (2024), he threw seven interceptions in 12 games. He also threw 29 touchdown passes. Texas 30, Ole Miss 27: The Longhorns are getting less for their NIL money than any other program. But just because you have a big-bucks payroll doesn't mean you have a big-play offense. Texas has scored fewer than 24 points in four of its six games. ADAMS: Tennessee football should be well aware of South Carolina threat on road And the Longhorns are on the verge of playing themselves out of the playoffs for a second consecutive season. But they might be catching the Rebels at the right time. A week after beating LSU, Ole Miss lost to Florida by 28 points. Now, it's coming off a 28-point victory over Missouri. Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 23: You might conclude that after five consecutive victories, the Wildcats are about to learn, as Smart said, that "humility is a week away." As accurate as Smart's assessment might be in general, it doesn't apply if you're playing Vanderbilt. Record: 59-14 (.793), 48-26 (.642) against the spread. John Adams is a senior columnist. He may be reached at 865-342-6284 or john.adams@knoxnews.com. Tennessee is facing one of its scariest tests of the season this weekend. After dominating Alabama last weekend in Knoxville, the Vols are set to head to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against South Carolina. It's a classic trap game for Tennessee in a stadium that's been a house of horrors for the program over the last two decades (the Vols are just 2-6 in Columbia since 2008, and one of those wins came in 2020 when fan attendance was limited due to Covid). South Carolina is coming off a bye week after a big road win against Florida earlier this month. ESPN's Greg McElroy picks winner of Tennessee vs South Carolina ESPN's Greg McElroy, who called the Vols' win over Alabama last weekend, thinks Tennessee will falter in Columbia on Saturday. McElroy has South Carolina beating Tennessee 27-24. “Can South Carolina stop the run that keeps Tennessee on schedule?” said McElroy. “Tennessee has 46 runs of 10 or more yards. That's top nine in the country, and Josh Heupel's teams are 71-9 when they run for 150 yards or more. Look, South Carolina is pretty stingy on those runs. So this is strength against strength, and the pick kind of tilts on whether Tennessee's quarterback can hold up his end of the bargain. “I'm going to take South Carolina to win this game 27-24. I think they're going to win on the ground. They're also coming off a bye. Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama. They looked amazing doing it, but we've seen teams elevate and then come back to earth the following week, and I think that could happen for Tennessee right here. Because (Matt) Fuller and (LaNorris) Sellers are going to get yards when that first defender misses. Tennessee's linebackers cannot afford to miss in this game. So that (Fuller and Sellers) will keep the Gamecocks out of third and long — which is where Tennessee's sacks live. It shrinks those pass rushing opportunities that are Tennessee's very best weapon.” “Tennessee's defense is amazing,” added McElroy. “They're sixth in points per drive. They're gonna make this thing super tight. But I just lean towards the Gamecocks in this game and the potential flat spot for the Volunteers — even though they bring the better defense into the matchup. The Gamecocks bring a run game and receivers that can win one-on-one. So we will take the Gamecocks.” Vols fans won't love that pick, but it's hard to blame McElroy, who has been pretty accurate with his predictions this season, based on Tennessee's past history in Columbia. picks.blurb: 'I really don't want to do this' - Former Georgia QB Aaron Murray predicts the winner of Tennessee vs South Carolina Skip to content NFL Close Menu All NFL Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks College Football Close Menu All College Football Alabama Crimson Tide Auburn Tigers Florida Gators Georgia Bulldogs Miami Hurricanes Michigan Wolverines Notre Dame Fighting Irish Ohio State Buckeyes Oklahoma Sooners Ole Miss Rebels Penn State Nittany Lions Tennessee Volunteers Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Draft Simulator Trade Simulator Toggle Mobile Navigation Home The Tennessee Vols will be looking for their first win in Columbia since 2020 on Saturday against the South Carolina Gamecocks. Tennessee is set to take on South Carolina on Saturday in Columbia. The Vols are coming off an emotional win over Alabama. And that win over Alabama combined with Tennessee's poor track record in Williams-Brice Stadium (UT is 2-6 in its last eight games in Columbia) has led to the Vols being put on upset alert this weekend by, well, almost everyone. ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, picked South Carolina to beat Tennessee 27-24 . Former Georgia quarterback Aaron Murray, who is also an ESPN analyst, is making a similar prediction. Murray has South Carolina beating Tennessee 24-21. “So it comes down to picking this football game,” said Murray. “I really don't want to do this. I wish I could just not do it, but I've got to. South Carolina 24, Tennessee 21. I'm doing it because I love both teams. And what have we learned this year? Teams coming off an emotional win do not perform well the next week. Tennessee's coming off an emotional win. South Carolina's coming off a bye. The game is in South Carolina. You fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me. We've been doing this all year. It feels like every big time game in college football, the winner loses the next week — especially if it's on the road.” “I love both teams,” added Murray. “… I'm just going with what history has told us this season. Tennessee had an emotional win against Bama. Smoking those cigars all night does not bode well for [recovery] the next day. So they're going on the road. South Carolina's healthy and coming off the bye. South Carolina wins.” I'm sure there will be some analysts here and there who pick Tennessee to win this game, but it seems like the majority of folks are picking South Carolina to come out on top. Tennessee has a big concern that's quietly developing and no one's talking about it, but it could be a big problem by the end of the season Josh Heupel and the Tennessee Volunteers have a potential problem quietly developing this season. The Sooners were in control of the Wildcats for most of the game before their offense fell apart late. OU is dealing with a plethora of offensive line injuries and John Mateer's turnover issues reappeared against UK. This week, the Sooners hit the road again. "We've got to get off the mat and got to go to Starkville," OU coach Brent Venables said. "It's a very unforgiving league." The Sooners travel to face Mississippi State on Saturday at Davis Wade Stadium. The game will be the first-ever meeting between the two programs. Bulldogs coach Jeff Lebby served as OU's offensive coordinator for two seasons from 2022-2023. In Year 3 at the helm, Lebby's two SEC wins through four conference games are already the most of his tenure. Before injuring his foot in a win over Missouri and playing through visible pain against Alabama, Taylor was a legit Heisman Trophy contender. The sophomore has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns and four interceptions. But he didn't play in this past Saturday's loss to LSU. His status will be the biggest storyline this week. The case for Mississippi State: If Taylor and leading rusher Fluff Bothwell return from injury, Lebby's offense should get back to its high-flying ways. And if the Bulldogs' defense can force John Mateer, who has turned the ball over nine times in six games, into mistakes they should win. The case for OU: The Sooners get healthy on the offensive line and Mateer takes better care of the football. Coach Brent Venables said last week star left tackle Michael Fasusi was close to a return and it'd be huge if OU could finally get him back. The Sooners' defense played great, once again, against Kentucky. If that side of the ball can force more turnovers, OU has a good shot. away.blurb: "We had plenty of opportunities there late into the third quarter to knock them out. We just weren't able to get it done.” With Michael Fasusi, Heath Ozaeta and Eddy Pierre-Louis out due to injury, Fodje was already playing out of position on a line filled with backups. Now, he was in clear pain. “I just listen to the trainers and him, what he’s telling them,” Venables said. “Some guys try to battle through that because they’re able to. He did all he could. If the trainers come over and say somebody’s out or somebody’s up, it goes according to what they say.” “That's just football,” offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle said of the offensive line. “We had opportunities there at the end of the game to go win the football game, and I got to be better in those moments and those situations, putting those guys in a position to be successful, regardless of who's out there. “Whatever 11 we have out there, it is my sole responsibility to put those kids in position to go be successful,” Arbuckle said. “Move the ball down the field, capitalize in those situations, those opportunities, regardless of who was out there. I have to be really good about putting those guys in position to go make the plays, to win the football game. Multiple injuries on the offensive line were a critical factor in the team's late-game collapse. Offensive lineman Ryan Fodje played through an injury, allowing two sacks on a key fourth-quarter drive. Quarterback John Mateer threw three interceptions, including a costly pick-six with just over a minute remaining. NORMAN — Around the midpoint of the third quarter, Ryan Fodje was hurt. Clearly in pain, the second-year Oklahoma offensive lineman limped off the field. Already down three linemen, the training staff re-taped Fodje’s right leg on the sideline and he was back in the game shortly afterward. The Sooners’ offensive line , which held its own for most of Saturday night, unraveled late. Fodje, who struggled to move, allowed two sacks on a critical drive early in the fourth quarter. OU’s offensive line injuries and lack of depth was its fatal flaw in a 21-13 loss to No. 17 Kentucky in which the Sooners outplayed the Wildcats for almost three quarters. With the loss, OU fell to 3-3. The Sooners outgained Kentucky 346-230 but their offense failed to move the ball with any efficiency late due to a decimated offensive line and overall inconsistent decisions. “They made the plays when they needed to, and we weren't able to get it done as a staff or as a team,” said Sooners coach Brent Venables, who is now 58 games into his tenure in which offensive dilemmas are a common theme. OU finally pulled Fodje late, placing Peyton Joseph at left tackle. Venables was asked postgame about the decision to continue playing Fodje even though he was clearly not 100%. away.headline: Oklahoma vs. Kentucky Injury Report: Sooners offensive line banged up
away.blurb: After initially being listed as questionable, Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta, a pair of players who have started a number of games for the Sooners over the last two seasons, were downgraded to doubtful. They joined fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis as doubtful. This comes after Head coach Brent Venables said Fasusi was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Well, it looks like we'll have to wait another week for Fasusi's return. With Fasusi, Ozaeta, and Pierre-Louis doubtful for Saturday, the Sooners will have another combination starting up front for the Sooners. Ryan Fodje will continue to start at left tackle with true freshman Noah Best at left guard. Jake Miakkula will be at center once again with E'Marion Harris at right tackle. That leaves right guard as the question mark. Peyton Joseph is probably the player coming off the bench to start for the Sooners. He's been a rotational player at guard this season, playing 47 snaps this season. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen has been ruled out for Saturday, putting Trystan Haynes in line to make his second straight start. For the Kentucky Wildcats , one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. He remains questionable for Saturday, and Pete Nakos of On3 says he'll be a game-time decision. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). Fasusi has missed the last four games after playing with a shoulder injury against UTEP. Ozaeta was banged up in warm-ups ahead of the Red River Showdown, but still played 59 snaps up front. The offense, playing without quarterback Kamario Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell, handed him a week full of hard questions. The first-year player from Tupelo was a two-time 7A Mr. Football in Mississippi, and the flashes are starting to show. Taylor did not play, so the falling tag is about his availability, not his performance. Lebby’s update made it clear the starter is not out of the woods. Lebby also explained why Taylor sat after pushing to return during the week . Mississippi State’s LSU Report Card Has One Grade That Stands Out The No. 16 Bulldogs fell 31-0 to No. 22 LSU Saturday and went 0-for-5 on fourth down. Here are three Mississippi State players rising and three falling after Week 7. Rising: Jett Jefferson, Cornerback Jefferson led Mississippi State with eight tackles and forced and recovered a fumble, the kind of game that keeps a defense breathing when the offense cannot move. The former East Central Community College standout missed most of last season with an injury, so watching him play every snap against an SEC passing attack is a real story. Lebby also noticed. “He’s continued to get better and better. A guy that has created a ton of trust to go play every single snap,” Lebby said in his postgame press conference. “So proud of him and what he’s doing, and gonna need that to continue.” Rising: Marcus Williams, Safety Williams finished with five tackles, two tackles for loss and a sack. The sixth-year Rice transfer picked up the first sack of his career against Missouri, and now he has another one against LSU. Williams has started every game this season, and he is becoming the safety Mississippi State can send after the quarterback without losing its footing in the back end. He also helped a run defense that held LSU to 90 rushing yards on 31 carries, under 3 yards per attempt. Few veterans have given this defense steadier play. Rising: J.J. Hill, Running Back Lebby made it clear that more work is coming if Hill earns it. “We’re gonna need JJ to have a really good week of practice. That’s the biggest thing,” Lebby said. “He does some great things, but man, it’s really hard to play in our system if I’m subbing guys in nonstop situationally. We’ve gotta create some trust, I love where he’s going.” Falling: Parker “Billy” Puckett, Quarterback Puckett deserves patience. The first-year walk-on made his first career start in Death Valley and went 16 of 26 for 121 yards with an interception. Still, Mississippi State came up empty on four consecutive fourth-down tries, including a fourth-and-goal from the LSU 6 just before halftime. If Taylor cannot play or is limited, backup quarterbacks Parker Puckett and AJ Swann could be called upon to lead the offense. That would place additional pressure on the offensive line and running game to help keep the Bulldogs competitive. Bothwell left the Alabama game after just one carry and has remained questionable heading into the LSU matchup. His absence would reduce the Bulldogs' options in the running game and make it more difficult to balance their offensive attack. If Bothwell is unavailable, Mississippi State could turn to other running backs, including Kolin Wilson and Xavier Gayten, for increased opportunities. Linebacker Jalen Smith and defensive linemen Diesel Moye and Trevion Williams are listed as out, while linebacker Zakari Tillman is also unavailable on the latest report. Those absences could leave the Bulldogs with less depth against an LSU offense looking to take advantage of its home-field advantage. And it comes at a less than ideal time as quarterback Kamario Taylor and the high-flying No. 19 Mississippi State (4-1, 2-1) offense comes to Baton Rouge for a pivotal conference showdown. away.blurb: The Wildcats are in desperate need of someone to step in for Oakley. He was the leading receiver at the position for K-State a year ago. This season, he is among the top players on the roster with NFL interest. During training camp, Klein said he hosted several NFL scouts who were on campus to check out Oakley. McCarthy starting for Giants Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Shandel Richardson Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas State Wildcats are expected to once again be without one of their key offensive players this weekend on the road against the Arizona State Sun Devils. K-State coach Collin Klein hinted that tight end Garrett Oakley could miss the third game of the Big 12 conference schedule. Oakley did not play in last week's game against the Kansas Jayhawks in the Sunflower Showdown at Bill Snyder Family Stadium. Here's what Klein had to say during his weekly press conference about the Oakley situation. "Probably unlikely, but we'll see," Klein said. "Day to day." Oakley missed the game because of an undisclosed illness. It gave more opportunities to sophomore Linkon Cure, who is among the most hyped players in program history. He is the first five-star recruit to ever play at Kansas State. While he has gotten off to a slow start, the Wildcats are hoping he can live up to the huge expectations. He has seven catches for 66 yards this season. Last week he caught two passes for 16 yards. The Wildcats need production from Cure because Oakley isn't the only tight end missing. Two weeks ago, it was announced that backup Will Anciaux would miss the season after sustaining a lower leg injury. Klein is also experimenting with moving left tackle Oliver Miller to tight end. That's where he played last week in the win against the Jayhawks. It is unknown if the move is permanent but that's where Miller will play this week. This was a move that was in the works because the Wildcats coaching staff was using him at tight end the past few weeks. A 6-foot-6 freshman, Miller has embraced the opportunity. He was a standout at Cherry Creek (Colo.) High School, where he was rated the No. 41 tackle in the country. Perhaps this could be a better calling for him because of his athleticism. The hope is Oakley is back in uniform sooner than later. He is a big component of the offense and is needed if the Wildcats are going to remain in the hunt for the Big 12 conference championship and College Football Playoff.

McCarthy starting for Giants Story by The Topeka Capital Journal Avery Johnson injury updates: Kansas State QB returns after leaving KU game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads MANHATTAN — Kansas State quarterback Avery Johnson returned to the game after missing one play that resulted in a touchdown. The quarterback was slow to get up after a 59-yard run that set up a four-yard rushing touchdown by Rodney Fields. Backup Jacob Knuth entered the game to hand the ball off to Fields with 13:46 left in the first quarter. Johnson lay on the turf for several minutes before being pulled up by the trainers. He smiled as he got up and had no noticeable limp . At the end of the 59-yard run, he stumbled before falling to the turf. Kansas ' Bryson Hayes returned the ensuing kickoff for a 95-yard touchdown to tie the game at seven with 13:04 left in the opening quarter. On Johnson's first play back, he completed a 45-yard pass to a wide-open Derrick Salley downfield. The Wildcats ran a designed run for Johnson two plays later. McCarthy starting for Giants Story by The Topeka Capital Journal Kansas State QB Avery Johnson laughs off injury scare in win vs Kansas Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads MANHATTAN — On the fourth play of Kansas State's matchup with Kansas , Wildcats quarterback Avery Johnson found a lane down the middle of the field and took off. Johnson was almost a blur and looked destined for the end zone, but it didn't go that way. An awkward fall to the turf ended his 59-yard run at Kansas ' 4, but no one at Bill Snyder Family Stadium cared that the play didn't result in a touchdown . Johnson lay on the ground for several minutes as trainers attended to him. Never mind the Wildcats' 17-game winning streak over the Jayhawks; it looked like K-State's star quarterback could be seriously hurt. "Y'all know that's my roommate; like, that's my best friend," running back Joe Jackson said. "I almost teared up at least a little bit." picks.blurb: Virginia Tech's Ethan Grunkemeyer leads the Hokies into Memorial Stadium, less than a year after he squared off against the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl at Yankee Stadium while playing for Penn State. In that game, Grunkemeyer threw for 260 yards and two touchdowns in Penn State's 22-10 win over Clemson. A third-year QB who committed to the Nittany Lions and James Franklin, Grunkemeyer followed his former Penn State coach to Blacksburg after Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech last November after the Nittany Lions parted ways with the 12-year skipper barely a month earlier. He has thrown for 1,984 yards and 15 touchdowns to two interceptions through seven games this season. Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech lead the ACC in passing yards , though the Hokies have played one more game than Darian Mensah and the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes. Clemson's passing game has been a complete contrast, to say the least. Through their first six contests, the Tigers have thrown a combined two touchdown psases between Week 1 starter Christopher Vizzina and former four-star freshman Tait Reynolds. The Tigers are second to last in the ACC in total offense with 340.7 yards per game while Virginia Tech ranks sixth (449.7) in the conference. Reynolds was 17 of 26 for 127 yards in Clemson's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern in Week 6. He has thrown for 943 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions entering his fifth start of 2026. Will Clemson football beat Virginia Tech? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Clemson as a 2.5-point favorite over Virginia Tech, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, gives Clemson a 55.9% chance to win. Virginia Tech has a 44.1% chance. The Tigers are No. 48 in ESPN's FPI with a 6.5 rating, which ranks 10th among ACC teams. Virginia Tech has a 6.6 rating that's one spot ahead of Clemson in ESPN's metrics. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Oregon State (6.0) in the FPI. Clemson football has longshot odds of reaching ACC title game entering Week 8 In ESPN's FPI entering Week 8, Clemson's chances of reaching six wins to qualify for a bowl game stand at 88.4%. The Tigers' chances of winning the ACC, however, are just 0.3%. That's down from 0.9% before the Tigers' 41-13 loss to the Miami Hurricanes on Oct. 3. Clemson's chances of reaching the 12-team College Football Playoff are 1.5%, which is down from 4.1% prior to the Miami loss and down from 22.2% entering the season. away.headline: Final Injury Report for Georgia Tech vs Virginia Tech: Who's in and Who's out for the Yellow Jackets?
away.blurb: The Yellow Jackets are going to be trying to pull off an upset against the Hokies today, but they are going to have to do so with some key players out. The final availability report is out for this game, and it includes the final status for running back Justice Haynes, who was listed as doubtful coming into Saturday, as well as offensive lineman Josh Petty and defensive lineman Landen Marshall. RB Justice Haynes and OT Josh Petty are going to be game-time decisions. If Haynes is unable to go today, Trelain Maddox and Chad Alexander would be the top options in the backfield for the Yellow Jackets today against Virginia Tech. Maddox is coming off the best game of his career last week against Duke. Riggs, the Yellow Jackets starting center, came back from an injury last week in the win over Duke, but was hurt during the game and did not return. He was not on the injury report this week and should be starting in the middle of the Yellow Jackets offensive line against what has been one of the ACC's best defensive fronts through the first part of the season. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/georgiatech as Final Injury Report for Georgia Tech vs Virginia Tech: Who's in and Who's out for the Yellow Jackets? . Kickoff time is getting closer for Georgia Tech and Virginia Tech. How do these injuries impact Georgia Tech today? There are two notable names not on the injury report this week and those are Jameson Riggs and Noah Carter. Carter has been perhaps the Yellow Jackets' most consistent pass rusher (although the pass rush has not been very good), and without Walker, Boyd, or Hoffler to get after the quarterback, Carter is going to be relied on to put pressure on Hokies QB Ethan Grunkemeyer, and Virginia Tech's offensive line has not been one of the best in the ACC so far this season. As poorly as the season started for Georgia Tech, a win on the road against the Hokies would be something that could potentially start to turn their season around. The Yellow Jackets have only one conference loss and with the ACC looking wide open after Miami, Georgia Tech can star to build some momentum that could get them to their fourth consecutive bowl appearance under Brent Key. away.blurb: Brody Meadows' Potential Return Could Bolster Virginia Tech's Injury-Hit Offensive Line Skip to main content SI.COM BLACKSBURG — Virginia Tech 's offensive line has been dealt a great deal of change due to several injuries, which has left younger players to take on larger roles. As the Hokies look to find stability up front, the potential return of fifth-year senior Brody Meadows could provide a much-needed presence. The outlook on Meadows' return is trending in the right direction, according to head coach James Franklin, who said Wednesday that the veteran lineman could factor into Saturday's game against Georgia Tech . With Virginia Tech working through injuries to Justin Terry, Johnny Garrett and Montavious Cunningham along the offensive line, Franklin emphasized the value of having an experienced lineman available. Franklin mentioned that the coaching staff has been cautious with Meadows' return as the injury has continued to linger. However, Meadows is listed as probable on Wednesday's avalibility report ahead of Saturday's game against Georgia Tech. Franklin also said Meadows performed well in practice Wednesday and could factor into the offensive line rotation. "It wasn't just like telling the coach what he wants to hear," Franklin said. "I think he's excited about the opportunity to go out and help his team. So, you know, guys like that are invaluable." With Meadows listed as probable and younger lineman continuing to gain experience, Virginia Tech could have another experienced presence available up front against Georgia Tech. More from Virginia Tech Hokies On SI FOOTBALL Meadows, a 6-foot-7, 330-pound lineman from Bluefield, Va., has played in 28 games across his career. After missing the entire 2025 season due to a foot injury, Meadows returned to the field this season before suffering another injury in the first half against Boston College in week four. Through four games this season, Meadows has played 73 snaps and recorded a 66.6 overall offensive grade from Pro Football Focus. He has earned a 65.0 pass-blocking grade and a 66.5 run-blocking grade. "We may get Brody Meadows back, and Brody's played a lot of football, so, you know, there's a ton of value in that," Franklin said Wednesday. Beyond his experience on the field, Franklin had high praises for Meadows' attitude and the relationships he has built within the program. "I'm a huge fan of his," Franklin said. "He's well liked and respected by his teammates and the coaches." Franklin said he checked in with Meadows about how he was feeling Wednesday and was encouraged by the lineman's response. After practice, Meadows told Franklin he felt "fantastic," responding with a smile that coach believed was genuine. At a massive 6-foot-7 and 330 pounds, Meadows also brings size and length that is needed to compete along an ACC offensive line. home.blurb: “I’ve been around here a minute, and we’ve had some games like this over the years where I’m not real happy in the fourth quarter because we’re sloppy. You’re playing a bunch of guys (backups), and all of a sudden you lose your edge a little bit. I felt they never lost their edge. They played tough. It’s hard to shut people out.” “It’s hard to shut people out. They had three yards in the second half, and we played 90 guys or more, so played a lot of guys. I thought they (the backups) just kept showing up.” “We’re a work in progress. ... Devarrick Woods (who didn’t dress Saturday due to injury) is gonna help us. ... Kourtney Kelly was so happy to be out there again, and I think Vic Burley had his best game. He played stout.” “I’d just come out of the tunnel to go to the bus, and I saw those F-16s (flyover planes) coming. You don’t hear them until they’re past you, which is probably bad news for the enemy, right?” No sweat: Clemson football shuts out Charleston Southern. home.blurb: Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return That progress includes moving from the larger brace to a sleeve and pad. Vizzina is still working to regain his full range of motion, so Swinney's update stops short of confirming a return to game action. True freshman Tait Reynolds took over as Clemson 's starter ahead of the North Carolina game after Vizzina started the first two contests. Vizzina was completely unavailable against the Tar Heels, then dressed against Cal strictly as an emergency option. Swinney made clear just how limited that availability was. Clemson would have turned to Trent Pearman and likely Brock Bradley before asking Vizzina to play against the Golden Bears. This article originally appeared on Clemson Wire: Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina takes big step toward injury return Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings J.J. McCarthy starting for Giants Drew Landon, Clemson Wire Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Christopher Vizzina has not played since suffering a left elbow injury against Georgia Southern in Week 2. His recovery has taken longer than Clemson initially expected, but head coach Dabo Swinney offered an encouraging update following Wednesday's practice. "CV is still not 100%, but this has been the best week he's had since before he got hurt," Swinney said. "He's just gotten better and better. We thought it would bounce back a little bit quicker, but it's just been hard for him," Swinney said. "But he's gotten better. He's had a really good week, and it's just one of those things that's been day-to-day." "It would have been like we would have had to get through Trent and probably even through Brock before we got to him," Swinney said. "He was just still really, really sore." Through his two starts, Vizzina completed 14 of 23 passes for 102 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Initial odds for college football's top Week 8 matchups are out Getty Images Two weeks away from the first set of College Football Playoff rankings coming out of the wildest Saturday across the sport in decades, the 2026 season has delivered in a big way so far. For the first time in the 90-year history of the AP poll dating back to 1936, five of the top seven teams lost on the same afternoon, sparking a much-needed rebound opportunity for the perceived elites in Week 8. While next weekend's matchups within the top 25 fail to offer a litany of "good on good" games like last, the unpredictability of the sport this season continues to carry significant weight. The only unbeatens remaining at midseason are BYU , James Madison , Miami , Texas Tech , UCLA and Utah after most of the unblemished went down on Saturday. Could more fall in Week 8 to unranked foes? Let's take a look at the schedule and early lines. Odds via FanDuel Sportsbook. The big games No. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas (-3.5 ): Will the Longhorns rebound as a home favorite against the Rebels, or will Steve Sarkisian lose a third straight SEC game and bring more questions to the Forty Acres this season? It benefits Texas if defensive end Colin Simmons , who leads the country with 10.5 sacks, returns after being carted off against Florida , but his injury status remains unknown. Trinidad Chambliss is the SEC's top individual playmaker at quarterback and has already had his way against two nationally-ranked opponents this fall with impressive wins over LSU and Missouri . No. 6 Indiana (-7.5) at Michigan : Backup quarterback Tommy Carr provided an immediate spark for the Wolverines against Penn State , leading multiple second-half touchdown drives after being plucked from the bench ahead of Bryce Underwood . Manufacturing that same level of success against the defending national champions, who saw their nation-leading 22-game winning streak snapped vs. Ohio State , is a different task entirely. Indiana hasn't won at Michigan Stadium since 1967, which is perhaps why this opening line seems a bit on the low side. No. 11 Tennessee (-2.5) at South Carolina : Can Shane Beamer knock off another top-15 SEC opponent with the Gamecocks? He's had an extra week to prepare -- 3-4 overall at South Carolina in that spot -- for what the Vols bring to Williams-Brice Stadium in a pivotal matchup for Tennessee's lasting CFP hopes. The Gamecocks clicked for the first time all season offensively last time out at Florida after LaNorris Sellers accounted for five total touchdowns. These two have split their last eight meetings dating back to 2016. No. 14 Houston at No. 10 Utah (-5.5) : The Utes survived a Big 12 warning shot at Colorado on Saturday night and now get a red-hot Cougars squad hoping to occupy one of the conference's multiple seats at the CFP table. Houston held off Oklahoma State , 35-32, in Week 7 behind Conner Weigman's five touchdown passes. For Utah, protecting home turf means preserving its unbeaten record and strengthening a playoff résumé that needs its first quality win with BYU looming on Nov. 7. No. 18 LSU (-6.5) at Auburn : Alex Golesh and the Tigers just knocked the SEC's king off the throne and now comes the tricky part: doing it again at home with everyone paying closer attention. LSU's coming off a 31-point demolition of Mississippi State and knows the margin for error is near zero the rest of the way in SEC play. Was Auburn's win between the hedges a turning point for the program or this season's signature moment? We'll know more after Week 8 inside Jordan-Hare. Although Ole Miss just beat Missouri 31-3, Trinidad Chambliss had arguably his worst game of the season, frequently missing throws and putting up just a 65.7% adjusted completion percentage. By Braden Ramsey Published: Oct 21, 2026 · 1:46 PM EDT There are only two ranked-on-ranked matchups on the Week 8 college football slate. While Houston-Utah will draw plenty of eyeballs, the SEC will be locked in on Ole Miss-Texas in Austin. The Rebels (5-1, 3-1 SEC) have only one ranked foe on their schedule after this battle with the Longhorns. If they can handle business on the road, they will feel very secure in their College Football Playoff positioning. Meanwhile, the Longhorns (4-2, 1-2 SEC) would be all but eliminated from the CFP chase if they suffered a third consecutive defeat. ESPN's Greg McElroy broke down the matchup on his Always College Football program. He believes Ole Miss becomes a real SEC Championship contender with a victory. “If Ole Miss wins, the national narrative is that Ole Miss is a real SEC title contender… they would be 4-1 in the league,” McElroy said. “Here's the detail that makes Ole Miss very dangerous: they don't play Kentucky or Tennessee this year… when Georgia comes to Oxford on Nov. 7, that game is essentially a play-in for Atlanta.” On the other side of the coin, McElroy thinks a Texas loss is something the nation is salivating about. A win, though, would thrust them back into the CFP picture because of their early season triumphs against Ohio State and Tennessee. “For Texas, a loss is the story the whole country has just been waiting to write… [and] the conference title's gone in October,” McElroy claimed. “If Texas wins, the national narrative is, ‘the most dangerous two-loss team in the country just reminded everybody why [they're dangerous]'… you beat Ole Miss… you now have three teams that you've beaten all power rated in the top 12.” Hear more from McElroy here: The Rebels and Longhorns kick off at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday night (ABC). away.headline: Kewan Lacy's Texas homecoming comes with an injury question for Ole Miss
away.blurb: "So I think every week is going to be pretty similar with him. I mean, you’ve got an experienced player that’s been in the system, right? So, you know, our responsibility throughout the week is to make sure we’re protecting him and taking care of him," Golding said on Monday. "It’s not like he’s forgot how to play football. So obviously the game plan is going to change a little bit week in and week out...But as far as, you know, the physicality of having to run the football, you know, versus scout team and all that, it’s not that..." For the second straight week, Kewan Lacy returns to familiar grounds. Last week, Lacy finished with 122 rushing yards against his former team, the Missouri Tigers. This week, Lacy returns to his home state of Texas. The Ole Miss running back attended Lancaster High School, located just outside of downtown Dallas. Lacy grew up a Texas Longhorns fan, and he'll have a chance to play against his childhood team, but his availability comes with caution. Keeping Lacy Healthy is a Top Priority Lacy has battled injuries all season. He missed one game with a shoulder injury, but even when Lacy was on the field, Rebels fans hadn't seen the star running back fully unlocked until Saturday. Lacy looked like his 2025 self against the Tigers. Lacy and Ole Miss would love to build on that momentum against Texas. But Pete Golding is remaining cautious with Lacy and his workload throughout the week. Lacy handled 306 carries last season. The Rebels leaned on him more than they'd like, so the coaching staff appears much more cautious with Lacy this season. He'll likely take it easy during practice and he'll be ramped up on gameday. This year, Ole Miss has someone who can take pressure off Lacy. Makhi Frazier is averaging 5.6 yards per carry on 45 attempts. Frazier's running ability makes life easier for Lacy and gives opposing defenses a different look at running back. As mentioned earlier, Lacy returns to the school he grew up watching. During SEC Media Days, Lacy said he wanted to commit to Texas, but the Longhorns never gave him an opportunity. Now, he'll be on the opposing side with his family in the crowd. “It’s going to mean a lot, just coming back home. I don’t really hold anything against Texas," Lacy said. "But it’s a hometown game, so I’m excited to have all my family, friends there.” If the Rebels are going to pull off a massive road victory, they'll need Lacy to have another dominant game. away.headline: The biggest Ole Miss-Texas advantage might be hiding in the trenches
away.blurb: One of the biggest advantages Ole Miss might have over Texas on Saturday isn't at quarterback, running back or wide receiver. It's along the offensive line. Through six games, the Rebels have allowed just five sacks, one of the better marks in the SEC. That's a stark contrast to Texas, which has surrendered 17 sacks while struggling to consistently protect quarterback Arch Manning. It's a difference that could become particularly important when the No. 7 Rebels travel to Austin to face the No. 19 Longhorns. Texas has struggled with pass protection throughout the season, but those problems have become especially noticeable against SEC competition. The Longhorns allowed six sacks in their 20-17 victory over Tennessee on Sept. 26, two in a 27-24 loss to Oklahoma and another five in last Saturday's 27-24 loss to Florida. That's 13 sacks allowed in three games , more than twice the number Ole Miss has surrendered all season. And it isn't as though the Rebels' offensive line has faced an easy schedule. Ole Miss has already played LSU, Florida, Vanderbilt and Missouri, with the offensive line allowing Trinidad Chambliss to operate one of the SEC's most productive passing attacks. Chambliss has thrown for 1,676 yards and 14 touchdowns, while the Rebels average 290.7 passing yards and 444.5 total yards per game. The offensive line has also helped Ole Miss establish a more consistent rushing attack in recent weeks. Against Missouri, Kewan Lacy and Makhi Frazier each eclipsed 100 rushing yards as the Rebels finished with 257 yards on the ground. That offensive balance could be important against a Texas defense that has been one of the nation's best. The Longhorns allow just 272.5 total yards and 17.8 points per game. They've also recorded 19 sacks and 46 tackles for loss. However, there's a significant question surrounding Texas' most disruptive defender. Star edge rusher Colin Simmons suffered a high ankle sprain during the Longhorns' loss to Florida and is reportedly expected to miss Saturday's game. Simmons leads the nation with 10.5 sacks and has recorded an incredible 16 tackles for loss through six games. To put his impact into perspective, Simmons accounts for more than 55% of Texas' sacks and nearly 35% of its tackles for loss. His potential absence would be a significant blow to a Texas defense that has often carried the Longhorns during their offensive struggles. Without Simmons, defensive coordinator Will Muschamp would need additional production from the rest of his defensive front, particularly Maraad Watson, who has three sacks. On the other side of the ball, Ole Miss' defensive front has started to show improvement since its disastrous performance against Florida. The Rebels have recorded five sacks and 13 tackles for loss in their past two games, including three sacks against Vanderbilt and two against Missouri. away.headline: Ole Miss-Missouri injury update: Key players’ statuses heading into Saturday
away.blurb: The most important news from this week's Student-Athlete Availability Reports for No. 13 Missouri at No. 9 Ole Miss was included in the initial report with Rebels defensive back Edwin Joseph listed as out for Saturday's matchup. Since then, there hasn't been much movement on either side, and Thursday night's updated report was largely status quo. The only notable change for Ole Miss was reserve offensive lineman Enoch Wangoy being added to the out list. While Wangoy has not been a regular contributor this season, his addition pushes the Rebels' total number of unavailable players to nine. Injuries have tested depth charts across the SEC all season, and Ole Miss is no exception. Fortunately for the Rebels, most of the players listed as out have been absent for several weeks, allowing the coaching staff time to adjust rotations and personnel packages. Ole Miss also continues to have just one player listed as questionable in tight end Hayden Bradley, while defensive backs Antonio Kite, MJ Preston and Ladarian Clardy remain listed as probable. If those three are able to play, it would help offset some of the losses in the secondary caused by Joseph and Nascar McCoy being unavailable. Missouri's report had six players listed as out, including running back Ahmad Hardy and safety JaDon Blair. Two more players are listed as doubtful, while linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr. and defensive tackle Sterling Webb remain questionable. Perhaps the most interesting names on Missouri's report are former Ole Miss players Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee . Both are listed as probable entering the weekend and appear to be trending toward availability for Saturday's game. It would not be surprising to see either player removed from the report on Friday or prior to kickoff as Missouri prepares for one of the SEC's featured matchups this weekend. home.headline: Johntay Cook faces Texas Longhorns two years after sudden dismissal
home.blurb: Once a five-star commit in Texas' 2023 recruiting class, Cook's career with the Longhorns came to a disappointing and surprising end. With his return to Austin now just days away, it's worth taking a look back at how things went down. Johntay Cook's Sudden Dismissal Came Out of Nowhere The Texas Longhorns will be reuniting with a familiar face during Saturday night's matchup against the Ole Miss Rebels in Austin. Former Texas wide receiver Johntay Cook II is returning to DKR for the first time since being dismissed from the program in the middle of the 2024 season. It's been nearly two years since he left the team and entered the portal. In the time since then, he's committed and decommitted from the Washington Huskies, spent one year with the Syracuse Orange, and is now in his first year with Ole Miss. Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian told the media in Nov. 2024 that Cook was no longer with the program, something that came up in the middle of the Longhorns' first season in the SEC. "We have nothing but respect for him and his family," Sarkisian said in Nov. 2024. "Wish him the best of luck in his future endeavors. ... It was mutual between the two of us." The announcement came as the Longhorns were coming off a ranked win on the road over No. 25 Vanderbilt, a victory that moved Texas to 7-1. The Longhorns were two days away from a home matchup with Florida, but Cook's sudden departure commanded some notable attention. It remains unclear what exactly the reason for Cook's dismissal was. The team obviously wanted to keep the reason in-house in order to avoid distractions. Earlier that season, Cook showed that there was reason for optimism after he caught two touchdowns in a blowout win over UTSA. However, he dropped a wide-open, would-be 62-yard touchdown pass in the SEC opener against Mississippi State two weeks later, and failed to see much playing time after that. He finished his two-year Texas career with 16 catches for 273 yards and two touchdowns. Johntay Cook Dealt With Legal Trouble After Leaving Texas After his departure from Texas, Cook went on a rollercoaster-like journey to find his next landing spot. Prior to the end of the 2024 college football season, he entered the transfer portal committed to play for Washington, but spent just a few days on campus before being dismissed from the program. He then got into legal trouble upon returning to his home state of Texas. Cook was arrested in Fort Worth in Feb. 2025 due on charges of interfering with public duties and theft of property between $100-$750, per reports from Fox 7 Austin. And 10 days later, Cook was back in a Texas county jail. He was arrested in Pottsboro, TX. for possession of marijuana under two ounces, per reports from WFAA. Despite the off-field concerns, Cook bounced back with Syracuse last year, posting 45 catches for 549 yards and two touchdowns in a career-best season. home.headline: Kewan Lacy's Texas homecoming comes with an injury question for Ole Miss
home.blurb: "So I think every week is going to be pretty similar with him. I mean, you’ve got an experienced player that’s been in the system, right? So, you know, our responsibility throughout the week is to make sure we’re protecting him and taking care of him," Golding said on Monday. "It’s not like he’s forgot how to play football. So obviously the game plan is going to change a little bit week in and week out...But as far as, you know, the physicality of having to run the football, you know, versus scout team and all that, it’s not that..." For the second straight week, Kewan Lacy returns to familiar grounds. Last week, Lacy finished with 122 rushing yards against his former team, the Missouri Tigers. This week, Lacy returns to his home state of Texas. The Ole Miss running back attended Lancaster High School, located just outside of downtown Dallas. Lacy grew up a Texas Longhorns fan, and he'll have a chance to play against his childhood team, but his availability comes with caution. Keeping Lacy Healthy is a Top Priority Lacy has battled injuries all season. He missed one game with a shoulder injury, but even when Lacy was on the field, Rebels fans hadn't seen the star running back fully unlocked until Saturday. Lacy looked like his 2025 self against the Tigers. Lacy and Ole Miss would love to build on that momentum against Texas. But Pete Golding is remaining cautious with Lacy and his workload throughout the week. Lacy handled 306 carries last season. The Rebels leaned on him more than they'd like, so the coaching staff appears much more cautious with Lacy this season. He'll likely take it easy during practice and he'll be ramped up on gameday. This year, Ole Miss has someone who can take pressure off Lacy. Makhi Frazier is averaging 5.6 yards per carry on 45 attempts. Frazier's running ability makes life easier for Lacy and gives opposing defenses a different look at running back. As mentioned earlier, Lacy returns to the school he grew up watching. During SEC Media Days, Lacy said he wanted to commit to Texas, but the Longhorns never gave him an opportunity. Now, he'll be on the opposing side with his family in the crowd. “It’s going to mean a lot, just coming back home. I don’t really hold anything against Texas," Lacy said. "But it’s a hometown game, so I’m excited to have all my family, friends there.” If the Rebels are going to pull off a massive road victory, they'll need Lacy to have another dominant game. home.headline: The biggest Ole Miss-Texas advantage might be hiding in the trenches
home.blurb: One of the biggest advantages Ole Miss might have over Texas on Saturday isn't at quarterback, running back or wide receiver. It's along the offensive line. Through six games, the Rebels have allowed just five sacks, one of the better marks in the SEC. That's a stark contrast to Texas, which has surrendered 17 sacks while struggling to consistently protect quarterback Arch Manning. It's a difference that could become particularly important when the No. 7 Rebels travel to Austin to face the No. 19 Longhorns. Texas has struggled with pass protection throughout the season, but those problems have become especially noticeable against SEC competition. The Longhorns allowed six sacks in their 20-17 victory over Tennessee on Sept. 26, two in a 27-24 loss to Oklahoma and another five in last Saturday's 27-24 loss to Florida. That's 13 sacks allowed in three games , more than twice the number Ole Miss has surrendered all season. And it isn't as though the Rebels' offensive line has faced an easy schedule. Ole Miss has already played LSU, Florida, Vanderbilt and Missouri, with the offensive line allowing Trinidad Chambliss to operate one of the SEC's most productive passing attacks. Chambliss has thrown for 1,676 yards and 14 touchdowns, while the Rebels average 290.7 passing yards and 444.5 total yards per game. The offensive line has also helped Ole Miss establish a more consistent rushing attack in recent weeks. Against Missouri, Kewan Lacy and Makhi Frazier each eclipsed 100 rushing yards as the Rebels finished with 257 yards on the ground. That offensive balance could be important against a Texas defense that has been one of the nation's best. The Longhorns allow just 272.5 total yards and 17.8 points per game. They've also recorded 19 sacks and 46 tackles for loss. However, there's a significant question surrounding Texas' most disruptive defender. Star edge rusher Colin Simmons suffered a high ankle sprain during the Longhorns' loss to Florida and is reportedly expected to miss Saturday's game. Simmons leads the nation with 10.5 sacks and has recorded an incredible 16 tackles for loss through six games. To put his impact into perspective, Simmons accounts for more than 55% of Texas' sacks and nearly 35% of its tackles for loss. His potential absence would be a significant blow to a Texas defense that has often carried the Longhorns during their offensive struggles. Without Simmons, defensive coordinator Will Muschamp would need additional production from the rest of his defensive front, particularly Maraad Watson, who has three sacks. On the other side of the ball, Ole Miss' defensive front has started to show improvement since its disastrous performance against Florida. The Rebels have recorded five sacks and 13 tackles for loss in their past two games, including three sacks against Vanderbilt and two against Missouri.
