picks.headline: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate
Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches
picks.blurb: Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Week 7 Fantasy Football Rankings World Series preview Champions League results J.J. McCarthy starting for Giants NBA breakout candidates Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 6:38 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will try to keep to momentum rolling as they enter their bye week after they host Vanderbilt under the lights on Saturday. Kentucky just played one of the best defenses in the SEC in Oklahoma , and now they get to play one of the worst as we previewed the Vanderbilt defense . On the offensive side of the football, the Commodores are led by five star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The offense has struggled but Curtis has shown plenty of flashes although he has a ton of room to grow. In our Vanderbilt defensive preview, we really centered it around Kentucky's offense and how they can exploit the Commodores defense. We are going to do the same here because this game is about Kentucky staying focused to enter the bye week with a 7-1 record. Jared Curtis has a rocket for an arm and is a big, physical runner. Kentucky head coach Will Stein said that Curtis plays like Josh Allen, but he made it clear he was not making the comparison. Coach Stein is correct though, Curtis can make unreal throws down the field and runs with physicality that is rare at the quarterback position. However, Curtis has a long way to become the dangerous player he is capable of. Curtis still needs to fix little things like footwork, staying in the pocket and taking care of the football. Curtis has one of the highest turnover worthy play percentages in the SEC, he will put the ball in harms way against this Kentucky defense that has been incredibly opportunistic this season. Curtis does not have much help around him, his offensive line has struggled all season. Vanderbilt allows the highest pressure rate in the SEC, which has led to Curtis being sacked a total of 10 times this season. However, Curtis is really difficult to bring down with his 6'4, 230-pound frame. His ability to erase sack opportunities is similar to South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers. Kentucky will win this matchup in the trenches, this deep defensive line unit will be able to get consistent pressure on Curtis. The biggest question will be how often they can convert those pressures into sacks, which they have been better at doing the last two weeks against Sam Leavitt and John Mateer. It will be a vital coaching point all week for the Wildcats to finish the play and get Curtis on the ground. If they allow Curtis to extend plays with his legs and erase sacks, it can lead to big plays down field as a passer or scrambling for a first down. Luckily for Kentucky, they won't have to see wide receiver Tre Richardson as he transferred to Louisville. Richardson lit them up last year down the field with Diego Pavia throwing all over this defense. I am sure a lot of the returning Wildcats on the defense have not forgotten that 45-17 beatdown last year in Nashville. This motivation will play a factor against a Vanderbilt team that is in a rebuilding stage. The Commodores receiving room is led by veteran Junior Sherrill, who is far and away the best weapon on this offense. Sherrill leads Vanderbilt in receptions, yards and touchdowns. He has four touchdowns on the season and all other wide receivers have combined for just one on the season. This is the guy to watch when Vanderbilt is on offense, they will force feed him the football. Vanderbilt offensive coordinator Tim Beck has one of the most unique offenses in the country and we saw how dangerous it could be last season. However, they lost their quarterback Diego Pavia who thrived in his system, they also lost their mismatch tight end Eli Stowers and the explosive weapon Richardson who transferred to Louisville. This is very much a transition year for this offense and it shows up on film. Kentucky has another opportunity to make a statement on defense after creating four turnovers and holding Oklahoma to just one touchdown last week. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 21, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Kentucky Football looks to keep climbing after Oklahoma win as Vanderbilt comes to Lexington. Kentucky Football continues to climb in the AP Top 25 Poll , moving up three spots to No. 12 after defeating Oklahoma, 21-13, in Norman. The Wildcats improved to 6-1 overall, became bowl eligible, and strengthened their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff in head coach Will Stein’s first season. The victory was far from perfect, as Kentucky’s offense struggled to find consistency after an impressive opening drive. However, the defense came up with several crucial plays down the stretch to help the Wildcats secure another impressive road win. Kentucky’s offense looked sharp on its opening possession, slicing through Oklahoma’s defense and setting the tone early. However, the unit stalled after that drive and did not score another offensive touchdown until 12:53 remained in the fourth quarter, when quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Willie Rodriguez for the Wildcats’ second touchdown of the game. Although the final score was relatively low, Kentucky’s defense also struggled at times in the first half. Safety Jordan Castell came up with a key interception when Oklahoma attempted a fake field goal in the first quarter, ending a promising Sooners possession. The Wildcats’ defense began to turn things around late in the third quarter when Ty Bryant intercepted Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer, giving Kentucky possession in Sooners territory. From there, the defense took control. Oklahoma recorded two three-and-outs and threw two more interceptions. Castell returned one for a pick-six, extending Kentucky’s lead to eight points, while Bryant secured the game-ending interception to seal the victory. While the game was sloppy on both sides, Kentucky found a way to finish strong. The Wildcats improved to 6-1, earned bowl eligibility, and continued building momentum as they pursue a potential College Football Playoff appearance. Now, Kentucky returns home to Kroger Field to face Vanderbilt, looking to avenge consecutive losses to the Commodores while losing three of four in the series. Kentucky fell 45-17 on the road last season after suffering a 20-13 defeat at home the year before. With Vanderbilt struggling through a disappointing season, the Wildcats will have an opportunity to extend their winning ways and continue climbing the national rankings. But if this last weekend showed us anything, it’s that upsets are commonplace this season, and Kentucky can’t afford to come out flat against a Commodores team starving for its first SEC win of the season. That, and Vandy did nearly pull off an upset over an Auburn team that just won at No. 1 Georgia. The Dores may be struggling, but they’ve still got an SEC roster. Vanderbilt Commodores (3-4, 0-4 in SEC) Vanderbilt has struggled through the first seven games of the season, and life after former quarterback Diego Pavia has been challenging. The Commodores finished the 2025 regular season with an impressive 10-2 record before losing to Iowa in the Citrus Bowl, ending the year at 10-3. However, the Dores have not come close to replicating that success this season. Vanderbilt suffered a disappointing 31-21 loss to Arkansas this past weekend. The Razorbacks entered the matchup on a 14-game Southeastern Conference losing streak, but they snapped that drought against the Commodores. One of Vanderbilt’s biggest challenges has been the development of 5-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The young signal-caller has shown flashes of his talent, but his inexperience has been evident. The drop-off from Pavia to Curtis has been noticeable, and Vanderbilt’s decision to start a true freshman at quarterback has come with growing pains. Through seven games, Curtis has completed 101/161 passes for 62.7%, totaling six passing touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also been sacked 11 times. Curtis measures 6-foot-3 and weighs 230 pounds, giving him the physical tools to develop into a quality quarterback. He can also make plays with his legs, recording 55 carries for 144 rushing yards and two touchdowns. However, his turnover numbers and struggles under pressure will be areas Kentucky looks to exploit. Vanderbilt’s other major weakness has been its defense, particularly against the run. The Commodores have struggled to establish consistency along their front seven, which could create problems against Kentucky’s rushing attack. The Wildcats have a three-headed backfield featuring CJ Baxter, provided he is healthy enough to play, alongside Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes. If Kentucky can keep all three involved, Vanderbilt could have a difficult time slowing down the ground game. Kentucky’s offensive line, known as the Big Blue Wall, has also looked impressive this season. If the unit continues to open running lanes and control the line of scrimmage, the Wildcats could have a significant advantage. As for Vanderbilt’s offense, Curtis has several weapons at his disposal. Senior wide receiver Junior Sherrill has emerged as Curtis’ primary target. The 5-foot-11, 200-pound receiver has recorded 41 receptions for 628 yards and four touchdowns so far this season. Junior wide receiver Ja’Cory Thomas provides another option at 6-foot-3 and 215 pounds. He has recorded 12 receptions for 195 yards and one touchdown. Vanderbilt also features junior tight end Jayvontay Conner, who stands 6-foot-4 and weighs 235 pounds. Conner has totaled 13 receptions for 146 yards, though he has yet to score a touchdown this season. Junior receiver Tristen Brown has added another option in the passing game, recording 12 receptions for 145 yards. In the backfield, Vanderbilt relies primarily on two running backs. Senior Sedrick Alexander, who stands 5-foot-9 and weighs 207 pounds, has recorded 61 carries for 270 yards and five touchdowns. Senior Makhilyn Young, at 5-foot-10 and 210 pounds, has added 52 carries for 216 yards and two touchdowns. For Vanderbilt to pull off the upset, Curtis will need to protect the football, make better decisions under pressure, and find ways to move the ball against Kentucky’s defense. The Commodores will also need to improve against the run to keep the Wildcats’ offense from controlling the game. Kentucky, meanwhile, will look to establish the run early, protect Minchey, and continue creating turnovers defensively. With the Wildcats playing at home and Vanderbilt struggling in SEC play, Kentucky has an opportunity to deliver another convincing win against a team that’s had its number. How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Vanderbilt Commodores Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Time: 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 24 TV Info: SEC Network Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as an 11.5-point favorite. ESPN gives Kentucky an 85.4% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 6-1 and bowl eligible, with its attention now turning toward the College Football Playoff. Under first-year head coach Will Stein, the Wildcats have shown they can win in different ways, whether through explosive offensive performances or clutch defensive plays in lower-scoring games. Vanderbilt, meanwhile, is reeling after falling to 3-4 overall and 0-4 in SEC play. Losing to Arkansas after the Razorbacks had endured a 14-game conference losing streak raises further questions about the direction of the Commodores’ season. Kentucky also has extra motivation after losing to Vanderbilt in each of the past two seasons. With the Wildcats playing at home, an improving defense, and a rushing attack capable of taking control of the game, I expect Kentucky to avenge those losses and earn a convincing victory. Chris Marshall suffered a right leg injury during the first quarter. He briefly returned to action for the Razorbacks (2-4, 0-3 SEC), but he appeared to re-aggravate the issue during a 28-yard screen pass on the final drive of the second period. away.headline: Who Vanderbilt Football's Backup Quarterback is With Blaze Berlowitz Injury
away.blurb: Vanderbilt likely did not envision either Muschamp or Elliott being the No. 2 quarterback at any point this season. The only way that would happen would be in the case of an injury to Curtis or Berlowitz. Tuesday, Lea announced that Berlowitz is out for about a month with a broken collarbone. "They both have the ability to go out and operate. Both represent the program, both have the confidence of their teammates, both had really good attempts for the starting job. So there's a lot of faith and confidence in what those guys bring," Lea said. When the quarterback competition began in the offseason, Lea made sure to say it was a four-way competition. Ultimately, he narrowed the competition down between Jared Curtis and Blaze Berlowitz fighting for the starting spot while Whit Muschamp and Jack Elliott fought for the No. 3 spot in the room. With Curtis entering his second game back in the lineup after missing the Georgia game with a knee bruise injury, Muschamp and Elliott will be up next on the depth chart for the next month. The depth chart lists the backup spot as Muschamp or Elliott. So who would go into the game first if Curtis were to get hurt again this season? "Whit would be the first in," Lea said. "But there's a real world where we would see both of them. And those guys are excellent. I mean, I can't say enough good things about them." Both Muschamp and Elliott appeared in Vanderbilt's trip to Athens a couple of weeks ago. Elliott was in the game for one snap, where he took a snap and ran a quarterback draw on the play. Muschamp entered the game on Vanderbilt's final drive, where he completed two passes for a total of 18 yards. Both fared well for the Commodores in fall camp. Muschamp especially had a quietly good camp that gave the impression that he was closer to the No. 2 spot than he was being the No. 4 in the quarterback room. Ideally, Vanderbilt would prefer to not see another Curtis injury in the coming weeks. But if that were to happen again by chance, Lea feels confident and has belief in both Muschamp and Elliott to run the offense. home.headline: Mailbag: How will CJ Baxter, other injuries affect Kentucky's playoff outlook?
home.blurb: Baxter was listed as a game-time decision on the pre-Oklahoma availability report. He participated in warmups and was running sprints on the sideline throughout the game but didn’t actually play. If Baxter does experience any setbacks this week, it does feel like holding him out against Vanderbilt with a bye week to follow would be a wise choice since Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes can still carry the load at running back. Vanderbilt is winless in SEC play, but Kentucky must still be on alert this week. This team needs a bye week to rest a variety of injuries, but I would be wary about holding anyone out against the Commodores who can play at other positions with less depth. The linebacker depth should be helped by the return of Alex Afari, but he did not play in Oklahoma, even after a judge made him eligible on Friday. The injuries for backup linebacker Antwan Smith and backup nickel back Jaden Smith appear to be long-term issues, so do not expect them back soon. Wide receiver Nic Anderson’s status will be worth watching this week too after he appeared to reaggravate his arm/shoulder issue in Oklahoma. For most of the history of Kentucky football winning in the home stadium of a traditional power like Oklahoma would have been the high point of a season. But for this Kentucky team, it wasn’t even the highlight of the month. Kentucky rode its opportunistic defense to a 21-13 win over Oklahoma to move to 6-1 on the season and 4-1 in SEC play. The No. 12 Wildcats are tied for first place in the SEC and seem likely to be slotted in a projected playoff spot when the committee releases its first ranking on Nov. 3, as long as Will Stein’s team takes care of business against Vanderbilt this week. Regardless of what happens from here, Stein has given Big Blue Nation reason to dream. The Wildcats are already bowl eligible, and that fact seems like an afterthought because of bigger goals in reach. Those bigger goals mean fans might not be simply content to ride the current high. To reach the playoff - and contend there - more improvements are needed. That balance is evident in this week’s UK football mailbag. You can submit questions each week via Twitter, Blue Sky or email. Waco Kid on X: Is this real life? What dimension did we magically travel into? It would be inaccurate to say Kentucky had never enjoyed a first seven games like these before, but this feels unprecedented for a couple of reasons. When Kentucky was 7-1 in 2018 with a winner-take-all-game for the SEC East against Georgia looming, the playoff only included four teams. It still didn’t feel like Kentucky had a shot to be included in the field. When Kentucky was 6-1 in 2007 with two top-10 wins on the resume and College GameDay headed to Lexington for the first time in program history, there was no playoff. Clearly in pain, the second-year Oklahoma offensive lineman limped off the field. Already down three linemen, the training staff re-taped Fodje’s right leg on the sideline and he was back in the game shortly afterward. The Sooners’ offensive line , which held its own for most of Saturday night, unraveled late. Fodje, who struggled to move, allowed two sacks on a critical drive early in the fourth quarter. OU’s offensive line injuries and lack of depth was its fatal flaw in a 21-13 loss to No. 17 Kentucky in which the Sooners outplayed the Wildcats for almost three quarters. With the loss, OU fell to 3-3. The Sooners outgained Kentucky 346-230 but their offense failed to move the ball with any efficiency late due to a decimated offensive line and overall inconsistent decisions. “They made the plays when they needed to, and we weren't able to get it done as a staff or as a team,” said Sooners coach Brent Venables, who is now 58 games into his tenure in which offensive dilemmas are a common theme. home.headline: Oklahoma vs. Kentucky Injury Report: Sooners offensive line banged up
home.blurb: After initially being listed as questionable, Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta, a pair of players who have started a number of games for the Sooners over the last two seasons, were downgraded to doubtful. They joined fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis as doubtful. This comes after Head coach Brent Venables said Fasusi was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Well, it looks like we'll have to wait another week for Fasusi's return. With Fasusi, Ozaeta, and Pierre-Louis doubtful for Saturday, the Sooners will have another combination starting up front for the Sooners. Ryan Fodje will continue to start at left tackle with true freshman Noah Best at left guard. Jake Miakkula will be at center once again with E'Marion Harris at right tackle. That leaves right guard as the question mark. Peyton Joseph is probably the player coming off the bench to start for the Sooners. He's been a rotational player at guard this season, playing 47 snaps this season. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen has been ruled out for Saturday, putting Trystan Haynes in line to make his second straight start. For the Kentucky Wildcats , one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. He remains questionable for Saturday, and Pete Nakos of On3 says he'll be a game-time decision. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). Fasusi has missed the last four games after playing with a shoulder injury against UTEP. Ozaeta was banged up in warm-ups ahead of the Red River Showdown, but still played 59 snaps up front. Here’s a New Mexico vs North Dakota State prediction. We will look at this from a betting perspective and determine the best New Mexico vs North Dakota State pick. North Dakota State Bison Betting Preview The Bison have been on a pretty good run this year so far; they’ve only got one blemish on the schedule. North Dakota State opened with wins over Jacksonville State, Fordham, Air Force, Sacramento State and Wyoming. The lone loss this year came on October 10 versus UNLV, but the Bison recovered with a win over Nevada last weekend for a 6-1 overall record. In the Nevada game, the Bison fell behind 11-0 in the second quarter but then rattled off three straight touchdowns for a 19-11 halftime lead. North Dakota State added a few more scores from there for a 31-17 victory in the end. QB Nathan Hayes was 19-of-25 for 153 yards and two touchdowns . Jackson Williams caught five balls for 58 yards in the victory. New Mexico Lobos Betting Preview Over on the Lobos’ side, they also have just one blemish on their schedule so far. New Mexico beat Central Michigan and Mercyhurst in their first two games ahead of a tough 14-6 loss to Oklahoma. The Lobos have since been on a tear, taking out New Mexico State, UTEP and Hawaii over the last three games on the way to a 5-1 overall run. Matched up against Hawaii last weekend the Lobos were down 10-0 by the end of the first half. New Mexico began their comeback with a TD in the third, then added two more trips to the end zone on the way to a 21-10 victory in the end. QB Toa Fa’avae was 5-of-10 for 59 yards and two picks. Scottre Humphrey had 15 carries for 90 yards and two scores. New Mexico vs North Dakota State Prediction I’ll stick with New Mexico but you could call this one either way. The Lobos played an ugly game versus Hawaii, bagging three turnovers and 16 penalties for 145 yards. New Mexico mustered just 94 yards passing, 5-of-13 on third downs and 16 first downs but the defense kept the team from imploding with 3-of-13 on third downs and two takeaways. New Mexico has 21 or more points in all five of their wins this year and 38 or more in four of them. As for North Dakota State, they held Nevada to just 15 first downs and 286 total yards with two takeaways in their latest win. The Bison defense has been great this year, giving up 17 points or fewer in six of seven games. This matchup could go a lot of different ways and it’ll be a fun one to watch.
